speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked	the Minister for Health what are the control measures to ensure that participating medical and dental clinics under the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) do not over-service and that fees remain competitive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: MOH has provided guidelines to the participating clinics to ensure that the subsidies are appropriately applied.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We review these guidelines from time to time to ensure they remain in line with our objectives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Charges may vary across clinics and patients, depending on multiple factors, such as the patient's condition, the length of consultation, the treatment and medication provided and the cost structure of the clinic, including rental and other overhead costs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We, therefore, encourage doctors and dentists to actively engage their patients, and vice versa, to address any concerns from patients on their treatment and charges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We also encourage clinics to display their common charges like consultation fees prominently in their clinics and provide itemised receipts to patients on request.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: These will make their charges more transparent to their patients and minimise misunderstanding.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Patients can also be alert to check their bills and alert MOH on any concerns that they may have and we will investigate and advise the clinics if appropriate.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: A few clarifications for the Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I have received quite a lot of feedback from residents and friends.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: From their point of view, it appears that many feel that prices have gone up.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, on the control measures that the Minister of State has outlined, I would like to ask what is the assessment of the effectiveness of these control measures.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Do we see the problem of possible over-claims to be widespread?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Since this question was filed, yes, indeed, there were two dental clinics that were suspended.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Because these are serious taxpayers' monies that are 	Page: 28 being paid out, we need to have a more proactive approach to this issue.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: While there have been some complaints alleging high fees or suspected over-charging, so far, we have not found any clear evidence of over-charging in these cases.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Given the considerable variation in GP practices and the autonomy of GPs to determine their charges, cases of overcharging can sometimes be very difficult to define.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Furthermore, like I mentioned in my reply, there are many factors that can result in the variation of the bill sizes and these include the patient's condition, how long the consultation is, the type of treatment, the type of medication and the complexity of the medical conditions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: All these will be taken into consideration during our investigation on some of the feedback from patients.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We also understand that some patients are quite concerned about being over-charged by their GPs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, if we compare this to the large number of CHAS claims, we have received a relatively small number of such concerns, although many of us do hear from some of our residents.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Because of that, we are unable to provide further details until the investigations have been completed.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have received feedback from residents that there are some GPs who have adopted the following practice where, for a follow-up visit to the GP, the GP now says that consultation fees must be levied if the CHAS subsidy is to be claimed, whereas previously, if the CHAS subsidy was not being claimed, then that consultation fee for a follow-up visit or for replenishment of medication would be waived.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I just want to confirm that this practice is not permissible if it is seen and is a ground for complaints.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: There are two different forms of subsidy according to the CHAS scheme, that is, there is a subsidy for acute conditions, as well as a subsidy for chronic conditions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For acute conditions, it is claimed on a per visit basis, and we do have a limit to the number of visits the patient can make within a month.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to chronic condition subsidy, there is a claim limit that a patient can claim for a particular year.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, if the patient has already exhausted the total amount that has been allocated, then the patient may have to come up with out-of-pocket expenditure.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to the Member's particular concern, it would be best if the Member can write to us so that we can investigate the matter and have more clarity on whether there is any misconduct or malpractice.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Precisely because it is difficult to ascertain, how would MOH look at this factor?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: There is also the danger of doctors over-prescribing, over-servicing.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I urge the Ministry to take a more active stance in approaching this issue.
